task:
FIX FIVE REVIEW FINDINGS ON PR #820 (purge P2b2a), review round 1. Branch codex/run-38794854189-1 at 16bb8a8a24706568a18458aca1999d168fa0634d. Change nothing else; do not weaken tests; do NOT change migration 016.

A1 (P1, floor bypass): abort-relation-* substitutes the relation's current size when the plan has no autovacuum_budget_bytes, and the plan generator never records one. Refuse abort with a clear code (for example autovacuum_budget_not_measured) unless the authenticated plan carries a valid rehearsal-derived autovacuum budget; when present, use max(budget, current heap+index bytes). Add the field to the plan schema as optional input that only a rehearsal-backed plan supplies (do not invent a default), and document that abort is unavailable until P2d's rehearsal figures are in the plan.

A2 (orphaned writer fence): admission only routes to restore-services when an open WRITER_FENCE_ENABLED coexists with an open BATCH_STARTED. Require restore-services whenever a writer fence (or SERVICES_QUIESCED) is open and was not opened by the current dispatch, for every non-restoration mode (delete-*, abort-relation-*, authorize, complete, and later rewrite-*). A dispatch must never adopt a writer fence left by a lost dispatch; abort must not return with application writes still disabled.

A3 (receipt truth): after restoration, report['writer_fence'] still says enabled/verified. Update the canonical writer_fence field to the verified restored state (keep writer_restore as detail if useful).

A4 (wrong next step after a partial abort): abort-relation-* always recommends rewrite-*. Derive the next mode from fresh target counts: recommend delete-<relation> when target rows remain, rewrite-<relation> only when both target counts are zero, otherwise status.

A5 (acknowledgement recorded as a fake FAILED_STOP): restore() records the owner's --acknowledge-failed-stop by appending a new FAILED_STOP event with integrity_failed false. Design 4.2 says the acknowledgement is recorded in the restore event's payload. Record it in the WRITER_FENCE_RESTORED payload (or the payload of the restore event 016 already accepts) instead, and do not append a synthetic FAILED_STOP. Keep the original integrity FAILED_STOP untouched (the P2a fence correctly keeps refusing on it -- an integrity failure needs separate repair authority; say so in the runbook). If 016's restore function cannot carry the acknowledgement in its payload, stop and report that conflict instead of inventing an event.

Add or adjust tests for A1-A5. Run: ruff check .; bash -n scripts/operator/actions/v3-derived-generation-purge.sh; python -m pytest -q tests/test_v3_purge_delete_dispatch.py tests/test_v3_purge_delete_operator.py tests/test_v3_purge_delete_transactions.py tests/test_v3_derived_generation_purge_operator.py tests/test_v3_purge_transactions.py tests/test_v3_governed_derived_purge.py; python scripts/operator/v3_production_deploy.py --operation authority-gate; the Semgrep command from .github/workflows/semgrep.yml. Allowed files: those already changed by this PR. End with files changed, what you did per A1-A5, tests run with counts.
